hypothesis: Verbatim real logs and audited PR relationships expose missing input and temporal semantics; isolating primary diagnostic messages should strengthen the lexical control without repository-specific keywords.
findings: An explicit closing relationship can name an unmerged proposal, and a merged linked PR can improve diagnostics rather than eliminate the underlying configuration problem.
All seven merged reference PRs follow the reported release; ancestor-only history cannot retrieve their landing commits.
The first Python traceback can follow the important native compiler diagnostics. Input extraction preserves the whole fenced log, excludes surrounding prose, and records character offsets.
Exception namespaces and trailing supported-item enumerations can dominate naive lexical queries; primary-message controls avoid that pollution without fixture-specific vocabulary.
FTS UNINDEXED provenance columns are not point-lookup indexes. A per-result verification scan was stopped after exhibiting quadratic cost; the verifier uses one corpus scan.
Basename-only path coincidences are retained as candidates, not accepted as repository coordinates.
limitations: Known linked PRs are incomplete relevance anchors, not an exhaustive gold set or proof of working fixes.
A null rank means outside an arm's first 100 results, not absent from the entire corpus.
One fusion rank outside the top ten regressed; both query modes remain available and the previous top-ten individual-arm hit is preserved.
The primary-message policy is an experimental control, not a demonstrated universally superior default.
No held-out retrieval results, cross-repository validation, paid agent runs, or hardware reproductions.
The sampled graph snapshots contain 8 to 31 dangling edges; omitted edges and unresolved coordinates are explicitly reported.

next.hypothesis: CBM code anchors combined with bounded post-version Git change history can retrieve useful merged PR evidence beyond the strengthened lexical controls.
next.first_test: Resolve corresponding symbols at the fixed upper graph commit and test native Git line history over the reported-version-to-upper-commit interval; compare with file-history and lexical controls. Record symbol moves and mismatches rather than asserting identity.
acceptance: Use only query logs, version scope, CBM results and ordinary commit-to-PR provenance to generate candidates; closing relationships remain evaluation-only.
Validate Git ancestry and exact PR landing facts; do not label background or proposed changes as released fixes.
Retain existing top-ten evidence and demonstrate an additional useful, manually inspected evidence path beyond the best lexical arms.
Reuse archived graphs through CBM; no custom code traversal, all-history graph copies, upstream writes, or automatic pushes.
Keep the held-out retrieval cases unqueried until a meaningful algorithm checkpoint.
unresolved_questions: How to query useful structural evidence when the traceback only contains wrappers or external library frames.
How to follow moved or renamed symbols across versions without confusing names with proven identity.
How to represent proposed unmerged remediation alongside landed changes.
Whether the available log contains enough context to distinguish model-specific failures such as issue 10772.
